calls.head: Wolf doesn’t own the Kings
calls.body: Wolf has been a wall against the Kings since 2023-24, well above his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if Wolf isn’t that wall tonight.

surprises.head: Calgary’s power play hit a new low
surprises.body: Calgary has one of the league’s least dangerous power plays. Even by those standards, this was a dry night: 1.9 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 6.6 and a league average of 7.8. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: The Flames beat the Kings
paras: Morgan Frost opened the scoring for the Flames early in the second. It was a busy third period. Joel Armia made it 1-1 for Los Angeles early in the period, and Matvei Gridin put the Flames ahead for good five minutes later. Yegor Sharangovich added the empty-netter with a little over a minute left to make it 3-1, and Los Angeles still answered. With the goalie pulled and just under a minute left, Mats Zuccarello scored his first goal for Los Angeles to pull the Kings within one, but the Flames held on.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Dustin Wolf made 29 saves for the Flames, and Anton Forsberg stopped 21 of 23 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Jake Middleton had the best night of anyone, even without a point.
Kevin Fiala picked up a ten-minute misconduct. The Flames improved to 9-10-1, sixth in the Pacific, while the Kings dropped to 5-11-2, seventh in the Pacific.
